[[upgrading_version_9]]

= Upgrading within Gradle 9.x.y

This chapter provides the information you need to migrate your Gradle 9.x.y builds to the latest.
For migrating to Gradle 9.0.0, see the <<upgrading_major_version_9.adoc#upgrading_major_version_9, older migration guide>> first.

We recommend the following steps for all users:

. Try running `gradle help --scan` and view the https://docs.gradle.com/develocity/get-started/#identifying_deprecated_gradle_functionality[deprecations view] of the generated Build Scan.
+
image::deprecations.png[Deprecations View of a Gradle Build Scan]
+
This lets you see any deprecation warnings that apply to your build.
+
Alternatively, you can run `gradle help --warning-mode=all` to see the deprecations in the console, though it may not report as much detailed information.
. Update your plugins.
+
Some plugins will break with this new version of Gradle because they use internal APIs that have been removed or changed.
The previous step will help you identify potential problems by issuing deprecation warnings when a plugin tries to use a deprecated part of the API.
+
. Run `gradle :wrapper --gradle-version {gradleVersion}` to update the project to {gradleVersion}.
. Try to run the project and debug any errors using the <<troubleshooting.adoc#troubleshooting, Troubleshooting Guide>>.

[[changes_9.9.0]]
== Upgrading from 9.8.0 and earlier

=== Potential breaking changes

[[kotlin_2_4_10]]
==== Upgrade to Kotlin 2.4.20

The embedded Kotlin has been upgraded from 2.4.10 to link:https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/tag/v2.4.20[Kotlin 2.4.20].

[[configuration_cache_and_problems_report_data_format]]
==== Configuration Cache and Problems report data format changes

The format of the data embedded in the HTML files of the <<configuration_cache_debugging.adoc#config_cache:troubleshooting,Configuration Cache report>> (including when <<isolated_projects.adoc#isolated_projects,Isolated Projects>> is enabled) and the <<reporting_problems.adoc#sec:generated_html_report,Problems report>> has changed in Gradle 9.9.0.
The reports themselves are not affected and look the same when opened in a browser.

This change only matters to tools and scripts that extract the embedded data from the report HTML files.
This data is an internal implementation detail of Gradle: it has never been a public API, and its format may change again in any future release, including patch releases, without notice.
If you have to extract this data, parse it defensively and expect to adjust your tooling when upgrading Gradle.

To consume problem data in a supported way, use the Problems API bindings of the Tooling API, as described in <<reporting_problems.adoc#tooling_api_clients,Tooling API Clients>>.

There is no supported way to programmatically inspect Configuration Cache problems yet.
The following issues track the development of TestKit APIs for this purpose:

- link:https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/35595[gradle/gradle#35595]: an API for verifying Configuration Cache compatibility and the inputs used by a build.
- link:https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/38223[gradle/gradle#38223]: an API for verifying whether a Configuration Cache entry was reused, missed, or discarded.

These APIs are intentionally focused on testing use cases.
If you extract the report data for other purposes, please comment on these issues and describe your use case.

[[relocated_root_project_settings_kept]]
==== Builds that move the root project directory now load their settings file

A build can move its root project with `rootProject.projectDir`.
When such a build was started with an explicit project directory, Gradle evaluated the settings file, found no project at that directory, and discarded the settings.
It then ran with a single root project at that directory, named after the directory and configured by any build script found there, as if the settings file did not exist.
With the Build Cache enabled, it failed with `Build cache controller already set` instead.
The Tooling API always sets a project directory, so every IDE run and every IDE sync was affected.

Gradle now keeps the evaluated settings and selects the root project for the build's root directory, so these builds load and run as written.

Two consequences are worth checking when you upgrade:

1. A build that silently ignored its settings file now uses it.
Configuration problems that were never reached before can surface.
2. `beforeSettings`, `settingsEvaluated` and the `Evaluate settings` build operation each fired twice in the affected case and now fire once.
Init scripts and build operation consumers that observed the second firing will see one.

[[gradle_in_non_project_directory]]
==== Running Gradle in a directory that is not part of the build now fails

When Gradle is invoked in a directory that lies inside a build's directory tree, other than the build's root directory, and is not a project directory of that build, `gradle help` and `gradle` with no task names previously discarded the surrounding build's settings and reported an undefined build:

[source,text]
----
Directory '/home/user/project/sub' does not contain a Gradle build.

To create a new build in this directory, run gradle init
----

Gradle now reports that the directory is not part of the surrounding build, and fails:

[source,text]
----
Project directory '/home/user/project/sub' is not part of the build defined by settings file '/home/user/project/settings.gradle'. If this is an unrelated build, it must have its own settings file.
----

`gradle <task>` has always produced this message in the same directory, so Gradle now behaves consistently whether or not you name a task.

The same applies to Tooling API clients that request a model for such a directory without running a task.
Such a request previously treated the directory as a separate build with its own root project, or failed with `Build cache controller already set` when the Build Cache was enabled.
It now fails with the message above.
Running a task in that directory through the Tooling API already failed this way.

If you hit this failure, pick whichever option matches your intent:

* Run Gradle from a project directory of the build, or from the build's root directory.
* If the directory is meant to be an independent build, give it its own settings file.
Running `gradle init` in the directory creates one for you.
* If the directory is meant to be part of the surrounding build, add it to that build's settings file with `include`.

Two cases are unaffected:

1. Running Gradle in a directory with no settings or build script anywhere in its parent hierarchy still reports an undefined build and still suggests `gradle init`.
2. Running `gradle init` in a directory inside an existing build still creates a new build there.

[[required_input_files_absent_nested_providers]]
==== Required input file properties reject absent providers nested in collections

Required task input file properties now fail validation when a provider nested in a plain collection or array (such as a `List` passed to link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/TaskInputs.html#files(java.lang.Object...)[`TaskInputs.files(...)`]) has no value.
This applies to `TaskInputs.files(...)` declarations and to required link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/InputFiles.html[`@InputFiles`] properties whose value is such a collection or array.
Gradle reports the failure as the <<validation_problems.adoc#value_not_set, Required value isn't set>> validation problem.

Passing several providers as varargs, such as `inputs.files(providerA, providerB)`, was ignored in the same way.
The collection and varargs forms now fail just like the direct form:

[source,kotlin]
.build.gradle.kts
----
val absent = objects.fileProperty() // no value configured

// Failed before this change, and still fails
tasks.register("direct") {
    inputs.files(absent).withPropertyName("p")
}

// Succeeded before this change, silently resolving to an empty collection; now fails
tasks.register("wrapped") {
    inputs.files(listOf(absent)).withPropertyName("p")
}
----

To fix this, make sure every provider in the collection has a value.
If the input is genuinely optional, declare it as such with link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/TaskInputFilePropertyBuilder.html#optional()[`optional()`] on the `TaskInputs.files(...)` registration, or with link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/Optional.html[`@Optional`] on the `@InputFiles` property.
Optional inputs are not affected by this change and continue to ignore absent providers.

=== Deprecations

[[kotlin_dsl_scripts_model_explicit_scripts]]
==== Deprecation of restricting the `KotlinDslScriptsModel` to explicit scripts

The `KotlinDslScriptsModel` is the Tooling API model that IDEs use to provide editing assistance for Kotlin DSL scripts.

Restricting the model to an explicit set of scripts by setting the `org.gradle.tooling.model.kotlin.dsl.scripts` Gradle property is now deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10.
The corresponding `KotlinDslScriptsModel.SCRIPTS_GRADLE_PROPERTY_NAME` constant in the Tooling API is deprecated on the same schedule.
Setting the property still works and emits a deprecation warning, so the behavior of such requests is unchanged in Gradle 9.x.
With <<isolated_projects.adoc#isolated_projects,Isolated Projects>> enabled, setting the property fails the model request, as it always has.

In Gradle 10, the property will be ignored, and the model will always be built for all the Kotlin DSL scripts of the build.

[[kotlin_dsl_zip_functions]]
==== Deprecation of the Kotlin DSL `zipTo` and `unzipTo` functions

The `zipTo` and `unzipTo` functions in the `org.gradle.kotlin.dsl.support` package have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10.

To create an archive, use the link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/bundling/Zip.html[`Zip`] task type:

[source,kotlin]
.build.gradle.kts
----
tasks.register<Zip>("packageDistribution") {
    archiveFileName = "my-distribution.zip"
    destinationDirectory = layout.buildDirectory.dir("dist")

    from(layout.buildDirectory.dir("toArchive"))
}
----

To unpack an archive in a build script, call `zipTree` inside a link:{groovyDslPath}/org.gradle.api.tasks.Copy.html[`Copy`] task:

[source,kotlin]
.build.gradle.kts
----
tasks.register<Copy>("unpackFiles") {
    from(zipTree("src/resources/thirdPartyResources.zip"))
    into(layout.buildDirectory.dir("resources"))
}
----

If you need to unpack imperatively from within a task action, inject link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/file/ArchiveOperations.html[`ArchiveOperations`] and link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/file/FileSystemOperations.html[`FileSystemOperations`]:

[source,kotlin]
.build.gradle.kts
----
abstract class UnpackTask @Inject constructor(
    private val archives: ArchiveOperations,
    private val fs: FileSystemOperations
) : DefaultTask() {
    @get:InputFile abstract val zipFile: RegularFileProperty
    @get:OutputDirectory abstract val destinationDir: DirectoryProperty

    @TaskAction
    fun unpack() {
        fs.copy {
            from(archives.zipTree(zipFile))
            into(destinationDir)
        }
    }
}
----

See <<working_with_files.adoc#sec:unpacking_archives_example, Unpacking archives>> in the Gradle User Manual for more details.

[[deprecated_configuration_cache_opt_out_properties]]
==== Deprecation of temporary Configuration Cache opt-out properties

The following Gradle properties were introduced as temporary opt-outs to ease the adoption of the Configuration Cache.
They let a build revert to earlier, more lenient behavior while the underlying build logic or plugins are being fixed.

These properties are now deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 11.
Setting any of them, to any value, emits a deprecation warning.

[cols="3,1,3"]
|===
| Property | Introduced in | Remediation

| `org.gradle.configuration-cache.inputs.unsafe.ignore.file-system-checks`
| Gradle 8.3
| Fix the build logic or plugins that perform file system checks, such as `File.exists()`, during configuration, so that they no longer cause unnecessary cache invalidation.

| `org.gradle.configuration-cache.inputs.unsafe.ignore.in-serialization`
| Gradle 8.4
| Fix the build logic or plugins that read the build environment while the task graph is being serialized, so that they no longer cause unnecessary cache invalidation.

| `org.gradle.configuration-cache.unsafe.ignore.unsupported-build-events-listeners`
| Gradle 9.0
| Convert the build event listeners passed to link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/build/event/BuildEventsListenerRegistry.html#onTaskCompletion(org.gradle.api.provider.Provider)[`BuildEventsListenerRegistry.onTaskCompletion`] into <<build_services.adoc#build_services,build services>>.

| `org.gradle.configuration-cache.unsafe.skip-task-logging-listeners-serialization`
| Gradle 9.8
| Fix the serialization issues of the task output listeners registered during configuration, or register them at execution time instead, for example in a task action.
|===

Use the <<configuration_cache_debugging.adoc#config_cache:troubleshooting, Configuration Cache report>> to identify the offending build logic.
See <<configuration_cache_enabling.adoc#config_cache:usage:input_opt_outs, Temporary Opt-Outs for Configuration Cache Behavior>> in the Gradle User Manual for the details of each property.

[[changes_9.8.0]]
== Upgrading from 9.7.0 and earlier

=== Potential breaking changes

[[kotlin_2_4_10]]
==== Upgrade to Kotlin 2.4.10

The embedded Kotlin has been upgraded from 2.4.0 to link:https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/tag/v2.4.10[Kotlin 2.4.10].

[[upgrade_to_asm_9_10_1]]
==== Upgrade to ASM 9.10.1

ASM was upgraded from 9.9 to https://asm.ow2.io/versions.html[9.10.1] to support Java 27.

[[upgrade_to_jacoco_0_8_15]]
==== Upgrade to JaCoCo 0.8.15

JaCoCo has been updated to https://www.jacoco.org/jacoco/trunk/doc/changes.html[0.8.15].
This changes the default `toolVersion` used by the <<jacoco_plugin.adoc#jacoco_plugin,JaCoCo plugin>>.
If you need to pin the previous version, set `jacoco.toolVersion = "0.8.14"` in your build.

[[upgrade_to_groovy_4_0_33]]
==== Upgrade to Groovy 4.0.33

Groovy has been updated to link:https://groovy-lang.org/changelogs/changelog-4.0.33.html[4.0.33].

[[task_logging_listeners_are_now_stored_in_the_configuration_cache]]
==== Task logging listeners are now stored in the Configuration Cache

Standard output and error listeners registered on a task's logging manager during configuration (for example via link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/logging/LoggingOutput.html#addStandardOutputListener(org.gradle.api.logging.StandardOutputListener)[`LoggingOutput.addStandardOutputListener`] or link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/logging/LoggingOutput.html#addStandardErrorListener(org.gradle.api.logging.StandardOutputListener)[`LoggingOutput.addStandardErrorListener`]) are now stored in the Configuration Cache and re-registered on a cache hit, so they receive the task's output as they would without the Configuration Cache.

Previously, these listeners were silently discarded and never received output when the Configuration Cache was used.

A listener that cannot be serialized is now reported as a Configuration Cache problem instead of being silently dropped, which may cause a build that previously worked to fail.
If your build registers such a listener and the listener is nonessential, you can opt out, restoring the previous behavior where listeners are dropped on a cache hit, and no problem is reported by setting:

[source,properties]
----
org.gradle.configuration-cache.unsafe.skip-task-logging-listeners-serialization=true
----

This property is a temporary opt-out, <<deprecated_configuration_cache_opt_out_properties, deprecated since Gradle 9.9>> and scheduled for removal in Gradle 11.

[[kotlin_object_singletons_in_configuration_cache]]
==== Kotlin `object` singletons keep their identity in the Configuration Cache

If your build stored mutable state on a Kotlin `object`, that state is no longer restored on a cache hit; move it elsewhere.

A Kotlin `object` (including `companion object` declarations) stored in the Configuration Cache is now restored as the same singleton instance.
As a consequence, only the singleton's identity is restored, not any mutable state it may hold.

Previously, each `object` was serialized as a regular bean and rebuilt as a _new_ instance on a cache hit, so `deserialized === TheObject` was `false`.
If you relied on mutable state surviving a cache hit, move it into a task property or another bean type that is serialized by value.

[[toolchain_invalid_installation_paths]]
==== Invalid toolchain installation paths now warn instead of failing the build

Unresolvable or relative paths in `org.gradle.java.installations.paths` and `org.gradle.java.installations.fromEnv` are now reported as warnings through the Problems API instead of failing the build with `UnsupportedOperationException: Cannot convert relative path ... to an absolute file.`.

These properties are optional configuration.
A valid toolchain may exist through another discovery mechanism, so an unresolvable entry should not prevent the build from running.

Common cases that previously failed and now warn:

- Cross-platform builds where a Unix-style absolute path such as `/opt/jdk-24` is treated as relative on Windows.
- Relative paths committed to `gradle.properties` in version control.

Correct the offending entries to remove the warning.
Builds that relied on the previous failure to surface misconfiguration should validate these properties by other means — for example, by running with `--warning-mode all` or inspecting the Problems report.

See <<toolchains.adoc#sec:custom_loc, Custom Toolchain Locations>> in the Gradle User Manual for details.

[[copy_sync_destination_directory_property]]
==== `Copy` and `Sync` destination is now a lazy `destinationDirectory` property

link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/Copy.html[`Copy`] and link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/Sync.html[`Sync`] now expose the destination as an incubating `DirectoryProperty destinationDirectory`.
For standard `Copy` and `Sync` tasks, `into(...)`, `setDestinationDir(File)`, `getDestinationDir()`, and `destinationDirectory` all configure or expose the same destination.

During Gradle 9.x, both `destinationDir` and `destinationDirectory` are registered as task outputs for binary compatibility.
The new `destinationDirectory` output is optional, allowing task types compiled against an earlier Gradle version that override `getDestinationDir()` to continue supplying the destination through the legacy output.
In Gradle 10, `destinationDirectory` will become the sole registered output.

Task types overriding the legacy accessors require special care during this transition:

* An overridden `getDestinationDir()` takes precedence when the task executes, even if `destinationDirectory` is configured separately.
* An overridden `setDestinationDir(File)` is not invoked when the destination is configured through `destinationDirectory`.

Either override can cause the legacy and lazy destinations to get out of sync, so task authors should migrate away from overriding these methods.

=== Deprecations

[[deprecate_implicit_parallel_model_building]]
==== Deprecation of implicit opt-in to parallel model building

Parallel model building lets Tooling API clients (most commonly IDEs during project synchronization) build project models in parallel.
Historically, it had no dedicated control and was enabled implicitly whenever parallel execution (`org.gradle.parallel=true` or `--parallel`) was enabled.

Gradle 9.4.0 introduced the dedicated `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` property to control parallel model building explicitly.
When that property is not set, its value is currently derived from `org.gradle.parallel` to preserve backward compatibility.

Relying on this implicit behavior is now deprecated.
When `org.gradle.parallel` is enabled and `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` is not set explicitly during model building, Gradle emits a deprecation warning.
In Gradle 10, the two properties will become independent, and enabling `org.gradle.parallel` without an explicit value for `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` during model building will be an error.

To avoid the warning and prepare for Gradle 10, set `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` explicitly to either `true` or `false`, for example in `gradle.properties`:

[source,properties]
----
org.gradle.tooling.parallel=true
----

Additionally, the transitional system property `org.gradle.tooling.parallel.ignore-legacy-default` (used by some IDEs during sync to opt out of the legacy default) will no longer be honored in Gradle 10.
Once `org.gradle.parallel` and `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` are independent, the flag is redundant, so Gradle 10 simply ignores it.
No action is required in Gradle 9.x; if you set it explicitly, you can remove it when upgrading to Gradle 10.

[[config_time_external_processes]]
==== Deprecation of starting external processes at configuration time with `ExecOperations` and Java/Groovy standard APIs

Starting an external process at configuration time with link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/process/ExecOperations.html[`ExecOperations`] or the Java and Groovy standard APIs directly is now deprecated.
This includes:

- `ExecOperations.exec` and `ExecOperations.javaexec`.
- `java.lang.ProcessBuilder.start()` and `ProcessBuilder.startPipeline(...)`.
- `java.lang.Runtime.exec(...)` (all overloads).
- The Groovy process helpers `String.execute(...)`, `String[].execute(...)`, and `List.execute(...)`.

This does *not* affect uses of the link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/provider/ProviderFactory.html#exec(org.gradle.api.Action)[`ProviderFactory.exec`] / link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/provider/ProviderFactory.html#javaexec(org.gradle.api.Action)[`ProviderFactory.javaexec`] providers (`providers.exec` / `providers.javaexec`) or a <<configuration_cache_requirements.adoc#config_cache:requirements:external_processes, `ValueSource`>> that runs a process inside, those remain the supported way to run a process at configuration time.

Starting an external process at configuration time in any of the deprecated ways is already an error when the Configuration Cache is enabled.
Because the Configuration Cache will be enabled by default in Gradle 10, Gradle now deprecates unsupported behaviors even when the Configuration Cache is not currently enabled.

Migrate to one of the following, in order of preference:

1. Move the process execution into a task, so it runs at execution time and benefits from build caching, up-to-date checks, and work avoidance.
Use an link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/Exec.html[`Exec`] or link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/tasks/JavaExec.html[`JavaExec`] task, or a custom task that injects link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/process/ExecOperations.html[`ExecOperations`] and runs the process in its task action.
2. For simple cases, use link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/provider/ProviderFactory.html#exec(org.gradle.api.Action)[`providers.exec`] / link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/provider/ProviderFactory.html#javaexec(org.gradle.api.Action)[`providers.javaexec`].
Prefer wiring the returned provider lazily to task inputs, and call `get()` only as a last resort.
3. For more complex output processing, use a <<configuration_cache_requirements.adoc#config_cache:requirements:external_processes, `ValueSource`>> that injects link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/process/ExecOperations.html[`ExecOperations`] (or uses `java.lang.ProcessBuilder` directly).
The same guidance about wiring the provider lazily to task inputs applies.

This behavior will become an error in Gradle 11.

[[deprecation_enabling_build_cache_from_build_logic]]
==== Deprecation of enabling the Build Cache from build logic

Enabling the Build Cache from build logic by mutating the start parameter, for example `gradle.startParameter.buildCacheEnabled = true` in a `settings.gradle(.kts)` file or init script, is now deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10.

Whether the Build Cache is enabled is determined by the Gradle invocation (`--build-cache` / `--no-build-cache`) and the `org.gradle.caching` Gradle property, and is not intended to be overridden by build logic.

Enable or disable the Build Cache with the `org.gradle.caching` Gradle property instead.
See <<build_cache.adoc#sec:build_cache_enable,Enable the Build Cache>> for details.

[[deprecate_implicit_dependencies_between_builds]]
==== Deprecation of implicit task dependencies between builds

Gradle now detects overlapping task outputs across the builds of a composite build.
Tasks in different builds that write to the same location no longer run in parallel, matching the behavior of tasks within a single build.

As part of this change, a task consuming the outputs of a task in another build without declaring an explicit or implicit dependency is now deprecated.
This will become an error in Gradle 10, matching the existing behavior for tasks in the same build.

See <<validation_problems.adoc#implicit_dependency,Implicit dependencies between tasks>> for details and possible solutions.

[[deprecated_startparameter_construction]]
==== Deprecation of creating and copying `StartParameter`

Starting in Gradle 10, constructing new instances of link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/StartParameter.html[`StartParameter`] will no longer be permitted.
It was never intended to be instantiated or copied by build logic, but the public no-argument constructor and the `newInstance()` / `newBuild()` methods made that possible.

The following have been deprecated for removal:

- the public link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/StartParameter.html[`StartParameter()`] constructor
- link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/StartParameter.html#newInstance()[`StartParameter.newInstance()`]
- link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/StartParameter.html#newBuild()[`StartParameter.newBuild()`]

The existing `StartParameter` instance for a build may be obtained via link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/invocation/Gradle.html#getStartParameter()[`Gradle.getStartParameter()`] instead of constructing or copying one.

[[deprecate_signature_as_artifact]]
==== Deprecation of `Signature` as a Configuration artifact

Starting in Gradle 10, link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/plugins/signing/Signature.html[`Signature`] will no longer implement link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/artifacts/PublishArtifact.html[`PublishArtifact`].
The following methods inherited from `PublishArtifact` have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10:

- `getName()` / `setName(String)`
- `getExtension()` / `setExtension(String)`
- `getType()` / `setType(String)`
- `getClassifier()` / `setClassifier(String)`
- `getDate()` / `setDate(Date)`
- `getBuildDependencies()`
- `builtBy(Object...)`

Furthermore, `Signature` will no longer extend the internal `AbstractPublishArtifact` class or implement the internal `PublishArtifactInternal` interface.
Code that dereferenced these internal types via `Signature` must be updated.
The `shouldBePublished()` method inherited from `PublishArtifactInternal` has also been deprecated for removal.

As a result, a `Signature` will no longer be permitted directly as an artifact of a `Configuration`.
Starting in Gradle 10, the <<signing_plugin.adoc#signing_plugin,Signing Plugin>> will no longer create the `signatures` configuration or automatically add `Signature` instances to it.

The `getConfiguration()` and `setConfiguration(Configuration)` methods on link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/plugins/signing/SigningExtension.html[`SigningExtension`] have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10.
Creating a configuration named `signatures` before the signing plugin is applied is now also deprecated.

[[deprecate_signature_constructors]]
==== Deprecation of constructing `Signature` instances

Starting in Gradle 10, manually constructing a link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/plugins/signing/Signature.html[`Signature`] instance will no longer be permitted.
All public constructors for this type have been deprecated for removal.

To sign files, use the `sign` methods on the link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/plugins/signing/Sign.html[`Sign`] task, or use the `sign` methods on link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/plugins/signing/SignOperation.html[`SignOperation`].

[[deprecate_sign_operation_signatures]]
==== Deprecation of `getSignatures()` and `getSingleSignature()` on `SignOperation`

The `getSignatures()` and `getSingleSignature()` methods on link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/plugins/signing/SignOperation.html[`SignOperation`] have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10.

Use `getFilesToSign()` and `getSignatureFiles()` instead.

[[deprecate_sign_classifier]]
==== Deprecation of signing files with a classifier

The following methods that accept a classifier alongside files to sign have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10:

- `Sign.sign(String, File...)`
- `SignOperation.sign(String, File...)`
- `SigningExtension.sign(String, File...)`

The classifier argument is ignored during signing and does not influence the resulting signature file.
Use the `sign(File...)` overloads instead.

[[unsupported_attribute_value_type]]
==== Deprecation of unsupported attribute value types

Attribute value types are limited to: `String`, `Boolean`, any subtype of `Number`, and any type that implements `org.gradle.api.Named`.

Passing any other type to link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/attributes/Attribute.html#of(java.lang.String,java.lang.Class)[`Attribute.of(String, Class)`] — or declaring an unsupported type as the type parameter of an `AttributeCompatibilityRule` or `AttributeDisambiguationRule` — now emits a deprecation warning and will become an error in Gradle 10.

The most common case is a plain Java `Enum` that does not implement `Named`.
Such types often work at first but fail later during dependency resolution, publishing, or Configuration Cache serialization — where the machinery assumes an attribute value can be reconstructed by name.

To fix a build affected by this deprecation, change the attribute value type to one of the supported types.
For enums, the simplest fix is to make the enum implement `Named` and return the constant's name from `getName()`.

See the <<variant_attributes.adoc#sec:creating-attributes, variant attributes documentation>> for the full set of supported attribute value types.

[[kgp_native_bundle_attribute_enum]]
==== Deprecation of using `KotlinNativeBundleArtifactsTypes` as an attribute value type

The Kotlin Gradle Plugin (KGP) 2.0.x line registers an attribute of type `org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.native.toolchain.KotlinNativeBundleArtifactFormat.KotlinNativeBundleArtifactsTypes` — a plain Java `Enum` that does not implement `org.gradle.api.Named`.

This deprecation is a specialized variant of the general <<#unsupported_attribute_value_type, unsupported attribute value type>> deprecation, called out separately so users can identify KGP as the source and remediate by upgrading the plugin.

To fix builds affected by this deprecation, upgrade the Kotlin Gradle Plugin to 2.1.0 or later.
KGP 2.1.0 and newer do not use a plain enum for this attribute and are unaffected.

Like the general case, this deprecation will become an error in Gradle 10.

See the <<variant_attributes.adoc#sec:creating-attributes, variant attributes documentation>> for the full set of supported attribute value types.

[[deprecated_macos_amd64]]
==== Deprecation of macOS on `AMD64`

macOS `AMD64` (Intel) is deprecated as a supported platform and will be removed from the <<compatibility.adoc#target_platforms, supported platforms>> in Gradle 10.

macOS 27 runs on Apple Silicon only, and the OpenJDK macOS/x64 port is link:https://openjdk.org/jeps/541[deprecated for removal], so JDK 27 and newer are not available for the platform.
Gradle is therefore no longer tested on macOS `AMD64` with Java 27 or newer.

To prepare for Gradle 10, move your builds to macOS `AArch64` (Apple Silicon).

[[changes_9.7.0]]
== Upgrading from 9.6.0 and earlier

=== Potential breaking changes

[[resilient_sync_reports_failed_operations]]
==== Resilient sync reports failed operations

Tooling API clients that query models through the incubating link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/tooling/BuildController.html#fetch(java.lang.Class)[`BuildController.fetch(...)`] method perform a _resilient sync_: failures are attached to each link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/tooling/FetchModelResult.html[`FetchModelResult`] instead of aborting the operation.

Previously, such an operation could complete successfully even when some of these model builds failed.
The failures were reported only through `FetchModelResult.getFailures()`, and the client still received a successful result.

Starting in Gradle 9.7.0, the operation is reported as failed when any part of it fails: `ResultHandler.onFailure(...)` is called, and a blocking `run()` throws, even though the partial models have already been delivered.
Because a single link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/tooling/BuildAction.html[`BuildAction`] loses its result in that case, clients should use a <<tooling_api.adoc#sec:embedding_phased_action_example,phased build action>> and read the partial models from the intermediate result handlers.

This aligns resilient sync with the reporting of `getModel(...)` and `findModel(...)`, and of task and configuration failures, so a sync in which something failed is no longer reported as successful.

[[publish_no_checksums_for_signature_files]]
==== Checksum files are no longer published for signature files

When publishing to Maven or Ivy repositories, Gradle no longer publishes checksum files (such as `.sha1` and `.md5`) for signature files like `.asc` and `.sig`.

A signature is itself an integrity artifact, so a checksum of a signature provides no additional protection, and the standard Maven publishing tooling does not publish these files either.
The signature files themselves continue to be published unchanged; only their checksum files are no longer produced.

[[project_cache_dir_no_longer_watched]]
==== The project cache directory is no longer watched

Gradle no longer watches the _project cache directory_ (the `.gradle` directory in the root project, or a custom location set with `--project-cache-dir`).
Because Gradle is the only writer to this directory, it keeps the virtual file system up to date directly, without relying on OS file system events.

As a result, a custom project cache directory no longer disables file system watching.
Previously, `--project-cache-dir` (or `org.gradle.projectcachedir`) was incompatible with watching: passing `--watch-fs` alongside it failed the build, and leaving watching at its default silently disabled it.
File system watching now follows the usual rules regardless of where the project cache directory is located.

This applies to the project cache directory itself.
Source-dependency check-outs, which live under the project cache directory but whose contents can change externally, remain watched as regular build directories.

See <<file_system_watching.adoc#sec:excluding_files_and_directories,Excluding files and directories>> for details.

[[kotlin_2_4_0]]
==== Upgrade to Kotlin 2.4.0

The embedded Kotlin has been upgraded from 2.3.21 to link:https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/tag/v2.4.0[Kotlin 2.4.0].

Starting with Kotlin `2.4.0`, the compiler no longer supports `-language-version=1.9`, which means the K1 compiler is gone entirely.
`2.0` is the new minimum compile target (and is itself deprecated, pointing at `2.2`).

From the `2.4.0` release notes:

- KGP requires a minimum Gradle version of `7.6.3`, fully tested through `9.5.0`.
- Support for Java `26` has been added.

Oldest supported `kotlin-dsl` plugin version is now `6.2.0`, which can be used to build precompiled-script plugins targeting a language level as old as `1.8`. Oldest supported KGP version is `1.9.22` which can be used to write Kotlin plugins targeting language levels as old as `1.4` and be used in Gradle versions as old as `7.2`.

[[kotlin_dsl_impldep_compilation]]
==== Kotlin DSL scripts can no longer reference relocated internal dependencies

Kotlin DSL build scripts (`.gradle.kts`) are now compiled against a prebuilt public API JAR from the Gradle distribution instead of the dynamically generated Gradle API JAR.

As a result, build scripts that import classes from `org.gradle.internal.impldep.*` (Gradle's relocated internal dependencies) will no longer compile.
These classes were never part of Gradle's public API.

If your build scripts reference `org.gradle.internal.impldep.*` types, replace them with the original library coordinates added as dependencies to your build logic:

[source,kotlin]
.build.gradle.kts
----
// Before (will no longer compile):
// import org.gradle.internal.impldep.com.google.gson.Gson

// After: add the dependency to buildscript or buildSrc
buildscript {
    dependencies {
        classpath("com.google.gson:gson:2.11.0")
    }
}
// Then import directly:
// import com.google.gson.Gson
----

NOTE: This change does not affect plugin projects that have `gradleApi()` or `gradleKotlinDsl()` among their dependencies. Those continue to use the full generated Gradle API JAR as before.

[[parameters_none_changes]]
==== Behavior and contract changes for `*Parameters.None`

The marker types used to declare a parameterless action — link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/workers/WorkParameters.None.html[`WorkParameters.None`], link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/artifacts/transform/TransformParameters.None.html[`TransformParameters.None`], link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/services/BuildServiceParameters.None.html[`BuildServiceParameters.None`], link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/provider/ValueSourceParameters.None.html[`ValueSourceParameters.None`], link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/api/flow/FlowParameters.None.html[`FlowParameters.None`] and `JvmTestToolchainParameters.None` — have been standardized.

1. **The configuration `Action` is now invoked even when the action declares `None` as its parameters type.**
Calls like `WorkQueue.submit(MyAction.class, p -> ...)`, `FlowActionSpec.parameters { ... }`, `ValueSourceSpec.parameters { ... }`, `BuildServiceSpec.parameters { ... }` and `TransformSpec.parameters { ... }` now always run the configuration block.
When the parameters type is `None`, the block receives the `None` singleton instead of being skipped.
Existing blocks that just configured properties on a real parameters type are unaffected; any code that relied on the block being silently skipped for `None` will now run.

2. **`getParameters()` returns the `None` singleton instead of `null` for parameterless actions.**
Inside a `WorkAction`, `TransformAction`, `BuildService`, `ValueSource` or `FlowAction` that declares `None` as its parameters type, `getParameters()` now returns the `None` singleton.
Previously it could return `null`.
Null-checks against the result are no longer required.

No source change is needed in typical builds.
If you have custom code that branched on `getParameters() == null` to detect a parameterless action, replace it with `getParameters() instanceof WorkParameters.None` (or the equivalent `None` type).

=== Feature previews

[[dependency_resolution_ordering]]
==== Opt into improved dependency resolution ordering

A new feature preview, `ENHANCED_GRAPH_ORDERING`, is available to opt into new dependency resolution ordering behavior that will become the default in Gradle 10.

With this feature preview enabled, Gradle will use a standard breadth-first ordering when using the `DEFAULT` sort order.
Gradle may optionally be configured to return artifacts sorted topologically, using the `CONSUMER_FIRST` sort option, which sorts artifacts earlier than those they depend on.
As usual, the `DEPENDENCY_FIRST` ordering is the reverse of the `CONSUMER_FIRST` ordering.

Notably, unlike the existing sorting methods, all sorting options in Gradle 10 will ignore constraint edges when traversing the resolved graph.

You can enable this feature preview in your `settings.gradle.kts`:

[source,kotlin]
----
// settings.gradle.kts
enableFeaturePreview("ENHANCED_GRAPH_ORDERING")
----

=== Deprecations

[[deprecated_software_model]]
==== Deprecation of the software model

The Gradle software model — including the `model { }` DSL, link:{javadocPath}/org/gradle/model/RuleSource.html[`RuleSource`] plugins, and the native and JVM component types built on top of them — is deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10.

This affects the following groups of public API types:

- The rule-authoring API in `org.gradle.model`: `RuleSource`, `ModelMap`, `ModelSet`, `ModelElement`, and the `@Model`, `@Mutate`, `@Defaults`, `@Finalize`, `@Validate`, `@Each`, `@Path`, `@RuleInput`, `@RuleTarget`, `@Rules`, `@Managed`, and `@Unmanaged` annotations.
- The component-model base API in `org.gradle.platform.base` and `org.gradle.language.base`: `ComponentSpec`, `BinarySpec`, `LibrarySpec`, `ApplicationSpec`, `LanguageSourceSet`, and related container, builder, and annotation types.
- The native component plugins: `c`, `cpp`, `objective-c`, `objective-cpp`, `assembler`, `windows-resources`, and `native-component`, along with their source-set, binary-spec, build-type, flavor, and prebuilt-library types in `org.gradle.nativeplatform` and `org.gradle.language.*`.
- The native test plugins `cunit`, `cunit-test-suite`, `google-test`, and `google-test-test-suite`, along with the rule-based `test-suite-base` infrastructure in `org.gradle.testing.base`.
- The `model`, `componentReport`, and `dependentComponents` diagnostic tasks.

Replace software-model-based builds with the current component model:

- For C and {cpp}, use the link:{userManualPath}/cpp_application_plugin.html[`cpp-application`] and link:{userManualPath}/cpp_library_plugin.html[`cpp-library`] plugins.
- For Swift, use the link:{userManualPath}/swift_application_plugin.html[`swift-application`] and link:{userManualPath}/swift_library_plugin.html[`swift-library`] plugins.
- For native testing, use the link:{userManualPath}/cpp_unit_test_plugin.html[`cpp-unit-test`] and link:{userManualPath}/xctest_plugin.html[`xctest`] plugins.

The new plugins configure components through ordinary Gradle extensions (`application { }`, `library { }`, `unitTest { }`) without the `model { }` block, integrate with the Configuration Cache, and support Gradle's standard dependency-management features.

[[deprecated_unsafe_isolated_projects_properties]]
==== Deprecation of `org.gradle.unsafe.isolated-projects*` property names

The Isolated Projects feature can now be enabled with stable property names that drop the `.unsafe.` segment, alongside a new incubating CLI option `--isolated-projects` / `--no-isolated-projects`:

|===
| Legacy name | New name

| `org.gradle.unsafe.isolated-projects`
| `org.gradle.isolated-projects`

| `org.gradle.unsafe.isolated-projects.diagnostics`
| `org.gradle.isolated-projects.diagnostics`

| `org.gradle.unsafe.isolated-projects.dangerously-ignore-problems`
| `org.gradle.isolated-projects.dangerously-ignore-problems`
|===

The legacy `org.gradle.unsafe.*` names are now deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
They continue to be accepted as aliases for now and currently emit no warning.
Update your `gradle.properties` and command-line invocations to the new names.

When both the legacy and the new name of a property are set — for example, the new name in `gradle.properties` and the legacy name injected by a plugin or CI script on the command line — an explicit `false` from either one disables the feature.
This guarantees that tooling which still opts out via a legacy property name keeps working after a build migrates to the new names.

See the <<isolated_projects.adoc#sec:enable_ip, Enabling Isolated Projects>> section in the Gradle User Manual for the recommended setup.

[[deprecated_custom_collection_types_with_cc]]
==== Deprecation of serializing custom collection and map types with the Configuration Cache

The Configuration Cache serializes a fixed set of standard collection, set, map, and queue types (such as `ArrayList`, `LinkedHashSet`, `LinkedHashMap`, and `ArrayDeque`) directly.
A _custom_ subtype of one of these types — for example, `class MyList extends ArrayList<String> {}` — cannot be restored as its own type and is instead restored as the nearest standard type, losing any state or behavior the custom type adds.

Referencing such a custom subtype from a task field or task action is now deprecated and will become an error in Gradle 10.

To fix it, use a standard collection or map type instead of a custom subtype, and store any extra data in separate fields.

See <<configuration_cache_requirements.adoc#config_cache:requirements:custom_collection_types, Custom Collection and Map Types>> for details.

[[changes_9.6.0]]
== Upgrading from 9.5.0 and earlier

[[v9_potential_breaking_changes_9_6]]
=== Potential breaking changes

[[agp_8x_incompatible]]
==== Plugins relying on removed Problems API internals are no longer compatible with Gradle 9.6

Several internal classes of the Problems API, such as `org.gradle.api.problems.internal.InternalProblems`, have been removed in Gradle 9.6.
Plugins that bound to these internal classes directly fail at build time with an error mentioning the removed type.

The most common case is Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 8.x, which relied on these internal classes.
To resolve this, upgrade to AGP 9.x, which only uses the public Gradle API and fully supports Gradle 9.6.
If the failure comes from another plugin, update it to a version that no longer uses Gradle internal APIs, or stay on Gradle 9.5 until such a version is available.

[[concurrency_primitives_prohibited_by_cc]]
==== Concurrency primitives can no longer be serialized by the Configuration Cache

Configuration Cache serialization now reports a clear problem when attempting to serialize most of Java's standard concurrency primitives.
This includes classes and interfaces from the `java.util.concurrent` and `java.util.concurrent.locks` packages, such as `ReentrantLock`, `CountDownLatch`, and `SynchronousQueue`.
Because the Configuration Cache enforces isolation between tasks, these primitives cannot be used correctly for cross-task synchronization.
Allowing serialization would silently give each task its own independent instance (for example, its own lock), so cross-task coordination would never actually occur — that is the bug this error prevents.

Previously, attempts to serialize these types could fail with exceptions such as `java.lang.reflect.InaccessibleObjectException`, without clearly indicating the underlying issue.
If your build requires shared, synchronized state, use <<build_services.adoc#build_services, shared build services>>, which are explicitly designed for safe coordination between tasks.

For a complete list of types that are incompatible with the Configuration Cache, see the <<configuration_cache_requirements.adoc#config_cache:requirements:disallowed_types, documentation>>.

[[v9_upgrade_to_kotlin_2_3_21]]

The embedded Kotlin has been upgraded from 2.3.20 to link:https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/tag/v2.3.21[Kotlin 2.3.21].

The default version of PMD has been updated from 7.13.0 to link:https://github.com/pmd/pmd/releases/tag/pmd_releases%2F7.24.0[7.24.0].

[[v9_upgrade_to_codenarc_3_7_0]]
==== Upgrade to CodeNarc 3.7.0

The default version of CodeNarc has been updated from 3.6.0 to link:https://github.com/CodeNarc/CodeNarc/blob/v3.7.0/CHANGELOG.md[3.7.0].

[[v9_upgrade_to_ant_1_10_17]]
